$schemaNote: The Capture Go onboarding ladder (Experience Brief item 2 / task item 2). Each rung pairs a board size with one tier from public/js/bot.mjs's BOT_TIERS (id must match a real BOT_TIERS entry -- play-app.mjs looks the chooser up by id, never hardcodes a second copy). introQuote/introSource are verbatim excerpts from this section's own lesson/glossary corpus, not invented copy -- see each rung's introSource path. A rung is 'cleared' the first time the human (Black) wins it by capture; play-app.mjs persists cleared rung ids to localStorage (see WEIQI_LADDER_PROGRESS_KEY) and unlocks the next rung in this array's order. All rungs stay playable regardless of lock state once unlocked -- nothing is ever taken away.

rungs.label: First Captures
rungs.introQuote: The central tactical unit is the liberty. A single stone in open space has four liberties, fewer on the edge, and fewer again in the corner. Connected stones share liberties, which is why groups matter more than isolated stones. When a move removes the last liberty from an opposing stone or group, the player captures it and removes it from the board.
rungs.celebration: First capture! You just did the one thing every game of Go comes down to: remove your opponent's last liberty.

rungs.label: Taking What's Offered
rungs.introQuote: A capture in weiqi occurs when a move removes the last liberty from an opposing stone or connected group, after which those stones are removed from the board. Capture is the game's basic tactical enforcement rule.
rungs.celebration: You beat Grabby! It never passes up a capture -- so if you won, you either avoided giving it one or out-captured it first.

rungs.label: Wider Board
rungs.introTitle: More liberties, more room to read
rungs.introQuote: Liberties matter because they convert board geometry into tactical pressure. A move may look quiet in territorial terms while still being urgent if it reduces a group from two liberties to one. This is why local fights in weiqi often turn on counting available adjacent points rather than on the nominal size of a group.
rungs.celebration: You beat Reaching! It builds toward open space instead of just grabbing captures -- on this bigger board, that takes real reading to beat.

rungs.label: Mind Your Liberties
rungs.introQuote: Atari matters because it turns a broad positional game into a forced tactical problem. When a group falls to one liberty, the next move often becomes urgent for both players: one side tries to capture, while the other tries to extend, connect, or create shape.
rungs.celebration: You cleared the ladder! Watchful counts liberties and rescues its own groups on purpose -- of the four bots here it's the one that fights back hardest, and round-robin play bears that out: this was a real fight, not a free win.
